## 49f7c594f382

**Reproduced shortcut — generated counts never exceed four.** The audited source hash is `463bd9278299092caeed0967db610397765f40d918207b90c2ceec4a3b3d28d6`. The intended rule keeps every color with an even total count, but generation chooses even counts only from `{2,4}` and odd counts only from `{1,3}`. Across 1,000 deterministic draws spanning all four band settings, every per-color count was 1..4 and every input had exactly three odd-count colors.

Therefore the simpler rival **“keep colors occurring exactly 2 or 4 times”** fits every generated draw. It also fits all canonical demonstrations, whose nonzero counts are only 1, 2, or 3. A legal 4×5 input with color 2 appearing six times and color 3 once is accepted by `self_check`; the selected Racket rule keeps all six color-2 cells, while the rival erases them. The selected-runtime receipt and complete probe are in `checks/audit/49f7c594f382/count-six/racket.json` and `checks/audit/49f7c594f382/count-six/report.json`.

The strict audit also found no task-local/frozen tests and no semantic contract. Defect lint reports a structural `palette_roles` mismatch, four dead helpful textures, missing `RULE_HASH`, and permissive scalar controls in `checks/audit/49f7c594f382-defect-lint/checks/49f7c594f382_audit_defect_lint.log`.

**Impact.** Current lessons cannot distinguish true parity from a bounded lookup over counts `{2,4}` and over-specialize to exactly three erased colors. No source fix was made; this is a findings-only audit.
